title: FLORA VETERANS DAY
full_story:
Flora American Legion Post #14 reminds residents about the observance of what was originally called Armistice Day.  It honored the end of World War I in Europe and was always observed when the war officially ended, on the 11th hour, of the 11th day of the 11th month.  Later, it transformed into Veterans Day, a day to honor the service of all who serve or have served in the U.S. Military services.  This year’s observance is on Wednesday in Flora at the Memorial in Library Park.

At 10:15 am all units assemble behind the American Legion on Mill Street.  Legion members will be joined by the Floyd Henson Jr. High School Band, the Flora Boy Scout Troop #8282, and the Shooting Stars Drill Team.  The parade steps off at 10:30 am and marches to the memorial.

The program includes the Marching Pups perform the Star-Spangled Banner.  The Pledge of Allegiance will be said, and Jim Earlywine will introduce the speaker Lee Ryker.  The Honor guard will lower the flag to half staff and fires a 21 Gun Salute and then Taps is played.  The tornado sirens will then sound at 11:11 am.  Following the ceremony attendees are invited to a meal served at VFW Post #3999 across from the Memorial.

title: NOVEMBER BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
Clay County is gearing up to help save lives ahead of the busy holiday season.  The American Red Cross is partnering with local organizations for a series of November blood drives.

First up, Clay Electric Cooperative is sponsoring its fourth annual “giving thanks” drive tomorrow.  That runs from 1 to 5 pm at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

Then, Flora High School will sponsor a drive on Friday.  The high school will host a scholarship-eligible drive in the school gym from 8:30 am until 2 pm.

Donors at these two drives will get a $10 Amazon gift card and 200 bonus points.

Finally… A major pre-thanksgiving push is scheduled for Wednesday, November 25th.  Donors can visit the Flora Odd-Fellows Lodge from 1 to 5 pm to donate blood.  Donors at this drive will get a American Red Cross, Wheel of Fortune Mug, while supplies last.

Organizers remind the public that the winter holidays traditionally see a dangerous drop-off in donations.

To be eligible to donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, and weigh at least 110 pounds while in generally good health.  High school students and other donors 18 years of age and younger must also meet specific height and weight requirements.  Donors must present a blood donor card, driver’s license or two other forms of identification at check-in.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

title: CLAY COUNTY RACCOON ROUNDUP
full_story:
The Clay County Farm Bureau is launching a “Raccoon Roundup” program to combat rising property damage from an increased raccoon population.

The initiative offers a $3 cash reward per raccoon tail for Farm Bureau members during the upcoming Illinois hunting and trapping seasons.

Two collection events will take place at the Farm Bureau office in Louisville from 6:00 to 7:00 PM this Thursday, November 12th and again on Thursday, January 14th.

Participants are limited to 33 tails per collection date and must present a valid DNR hunting or trapping license.  All harvests must strictly follow state regulations.

title: MARION COUNTY ACCIDENT
full_story:
Marion County Sheriff’s Deputies report that seventy-two-year-old Deborah Ruholl of Flora was traveling west on US 50 when she made a left turn directly in front of an oncoming eastbound SUV.

The SUV, driven by 48-year-old Michael Wasion, also of Flora, overturned onto its side upon impact.

Marion County Sheriff Kevin Cripps was among the first to arrive on the scene and personally assisted two occupants out of the overturned vehicle.  The Iuka Fire Department also responded to assist at the scene.

Emergency crews transported Wasion and two of his passengers, sixty-six-year-old Charleen Lister of Salem and seventy-seven-year-old Samuel Wasion of Flora, to Salem Township Hospital.  Lister was later flown from the hospital’s helipad to a St. Louis hospital for further treatment.

Ruholl later sought treatment on her own at Clay County Hospital in Flora.

Authorities say the crash was first reported at approximately 4 pm Thursday afternoon.

title: POLICE CARS ATTACKED
full_story:
A Mt. Vernon man faces multiple felony charges after allegedly wielding a knife to slash the tires of 10 police vehicles and subsequently attacking both a police officer and a hospital nurse.

Daniel Artis, 29, of Mt. Vernon, was taken into custody following a tense standoff.  According to the Mt. Vernon Police Department, officers responded to a report of tires being slashed at approximately 1:46 pm on Thursday at the Rolland Lewis Building.  The parking lot was being used for overflow parking while regional law enforcement personnel attended a training class nearby.  As the first responding officer arrived and exited his vehicle, Artis allegedly approached armed with a knife and immediately slashed the squad car’s front passenger-side tire.

The officer drew his firearm and utilized the squad car as a barrier.  Artis then moved to the back of the vehicle and slashed the rear passenger-side tire.  As backup arrived, the initial officer switched from his firearm to a department-issued Taser.  Following a foot pursuit, the officer successfully deployed the Taser, causing Artis to drop the knife and allowing officers to take him into custody.

While being prepared for medical transport, Artis bit a police officer.  Upon arriving at a local hospital for evaluation, he also spit on a nurse.  In total, Artis managed to damage 10 squad cars belonging to multiple regional law enforcement agencies, slashing between two and four tires on each vehicle.

Following his medical clearance, Artis was booked into the Jefferson County Jail.  Artis faces 10 counts of Criminal Damage to State-Supported Property, 2 counts of Aggravated Battery to a Nurse, 1 count of Aggravated Battery to a Peace Officer, and 1 count of Armed Violence.

title: IFB COLLEGIATE DISCUSSION MEET
full_story:
Sidney Stiers, of Williamsfield, took first place in Illinois Farm Bureau’s Collegiate Discussion Meet, held October 30th.

Stiers, a sophomore at the University of Illinois, is a member of the Knox County Farm Bureau and the University of Illinois Collegiate Farm Bureau chapter.  She will go on to represent Illinois in the national Collegiate Discussion Meet at the American Farm Bureau Federation’s Young Farmers and Ranchers Conference March 12th through 15th, in New Orleans.

In addition to a $200 cash prize, Stiers earned an expense-paid trip to the American Farm Bureau Federation’s Young Farmers and Ranchers Conference and the Illinois Farm Bureau Annual Meeting in December, as well as a $1,500 scholarship courtesy of GROWMARK, Inc.

The Illinois Farm Bureau Collegiate Discussion Meet evaluates participants’ ability to exchange ideas, solve problems, and work collaboratively in a discussion-based setting. Competitors demonstrate their understanding of agricultural issues while showcasing communication, critical-thinking and leadership skills. The competition includes opening statements, open discussion, and closing statements, with judges scoring participants on topic analysis, problem-solving, implementation of ideas, cooperative attitude and delivery.

This year’s event marked a record level of participation, with 33 students competing at Illinois Farm Bureau’s home office in Bloomington. Due to the continued growth of the competition, a Sweet 16 round was held for the first time in the event’s history, with the top 16 contestants advancing following preliminary rounds of competition.

Taking second place was Haley Bode, of Southern Illinois University, from Monroe County.  Third place was awarded to Rylee Skillman, of Joliet Junior College, from Will County, and Fourth place went to Alex Paul of University of Illinois, from Wayne County.

title: TATE MOVED
full_story:
Convicted killer Ray E. Tate was whisked away to an out-of-state prison this week, not long after the Fifth District Court of Appeals upheld his conviction and life sentence for the December 29, 2021 slaying of Wayne County Sheriff’s Deputy Sean Riley.

Officials with the Illinois Department of Corrections would only say that Tate has been moved from the maximum-security Menard State Penitentiary at Chester to an undisclosed out-of-state facility.  The move was facilitated through the Department of Corrections Interstate Compact.

title: 44 COUNTIES VOTE FOR SEPARATION
full_story:
Voters in 44 Illinois counties plus 11 townships in a 45th have now approved a referendum to consider separating from Cook County and forming a new state.

Eleven townships in Adams County joined Coles, Gallatin, Hamilton, Henderson, Macoupin, McDonough, Monroe, Piatt, Saline, Warren and Washington counties by voting on Tuesday in favor of a nonbinding ballot question that was previously approved by 33 other Illinois counties.

Illinois Separation Director Loret Newlin said six counties came in with less than 70% of voters saying yes.

“That was a little bit disheartening, but we are moving into a different part of the state than we were initially.  Our results were still very strong,” Newlin told The Center Square.

Newlin said voter approval ranged from 57% in McDonough County to 90% in one Adams County township.

“Hamilton was the strongest full county at 80%. The weakest one was McDonough which, frankly, I was concerned about whether McDonough would pass,” Newlin said.

Counties that pass the referendum do not actually separate from Illinois, but they signal that they want in on discussions to possibly form a new state.

Seven counties already have contact persons for separation referendum petitions in 2028.

The list includes Adams, where eleven townships voted in favor of the referendum on Tuesday by unofficial margins ranging from 79% to 90%.

The list also includes Kankakee, which Newlin said has potential, even though it is closer to Chicago than any county to vote on the measure so far.

“Again, we’re going to do it by township because they need three thousand or so signatures.  We’ll see what happens.  There’s interest, but is there going to be follow through?  I can’t predict that,” Newlin said.

Franklin, Tazewell, Vermilion, Whiteside and Woodford counties also have contacts for petitions.  Illinois has a total of 102 counties.

Newlin said people who support the referendum should not make their own petitions.

“All the petitions have to be uniform.  There are requirements that the State Board of Elections requires, and one of them is uniformity,” Newlin said.
